newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine police indictment for Jewish bomb upheld.
newsitem.headline: Argentine police indictment for Jewish bomb upheld.

text.p: An Argentine appeals court has upheld the indictment of four Buenos Aires Province police officers in a 1994 bomb attack on Buenos Aires' Jewish community, prosecutors said on Tuesday.

State prosecutor Eamon Mullen, investigating the July 1994 car bomb that killed 86 people and injured hundreds more, told local radio the Federal Appeals Court ruling was "a major step forward. It's a major boost for the investigation."
The bombers who carried out the attack on the AMIA, the cultural centre for Buenos Aires' Jewish community -- one of the largest in the world -- have not yet been caught.

But two months ago investigating Judge Juan Jose Galeano arrested 14 Buenos Aires Province policemen on suspicion of supplying the van used in the attack. Four were indicted for the AMIA case and the rest on unrelated racketeering charges.

Mullen said the four were jailed pending trial for the bombing. Commissioner Juan Jose Ribelli, Deputy Commissioners Raul Edilio Ibarra and Anastacio Irineo Leal and retired Inspector Mario Norberto Bareiro were considered "necessary accomplices" to the crime.

"They could face the same sentence as the author of the incident. They are now ready for a hearing," he said. "... Either these people carried out the attack or they handed over the van to an intermediary or they delivered it directly to the terrorists."

The text of the appeals court ruling describes the four as "primary accomplices" and quotes a witness as saying a man who looked like Ibarra told him before the AMIA bombing "something big is going to happen and you'll see it in the newspapers."

Argentina's police and courts have been criticised by Israel, the United States and Jewish leaders for failing to solve the AMIA bombing and a 1992 bomb attack on the Israeli embassy in Buenos Aires, which killed 29 people.
